mitigations.content: Make every firmware variant refuse any OTA that does not carry a valid signature chained to the baked signer root (fail closed when sigAlg is missing), and have publish-ota sign every push including the classical era.
mitigations.implementation_details: In otaTask replace the 'UNSIGNED ... proceeding' else-branch with a refusal in all three .ino sketches; ensure buildspec sets a signer era for classical builds and publish-ota always sends sigAlg/sigUrl/signerCertUrl. Re-flash devices so the first-flash image enforces the policy.

mitigations.content: Verify the OTA download server: fix the wolfSSL chain issue (load the Amazon intermediate/roots and enable WOLFSSL_VERIFY_PEER with SNI and domain check) and only accept URLs whose host is the workshop firmware bucket's regional S3 endpoint.
mitigations.implementation_details: Replace WOLFSSL_VERIFY_NONE in otaTask and otaHttpsGetToBuffer; bake the expected bucket host at build time and reject other hosts before connecting.

mitigations.content: Add a Mosquitto ACL that confines each device to its own topics: write dt/%u/#, read cmd/%u/#, using the certificate CN as the username (use_identity_as_username is already on).
mitigations.implementation_details: Add acl_file to both listeners in mosquitto.conf with 'pattern write dt/%u/#' and 'pattern read cmd/%u/#'; give the bridge its own rules. Device CN is already esp32-<serial>.

mitigations.content: Replace anonymous dashboard access: add a Cognito user pool (operator and per-event attendee sign-in), keep the unauthenticated role read-only, and allow mutations only to authenticated users scoped to their own device where possible.
mitigations.implementation_details: Add a user pool and IdentityPoolRoleAttachment 'authenticated' role; restrict CognitoUnauthRole to appsync:GraphQL on .../types/Query/fields/listDevices and getDevice; move migrateFirmware/getDeviceLog/getBrokerLog to the authenticated role.

mitigations.content: Remove updateDevice from browser-callable access: only the telemetry processor writes device state, so scope the guest role's appsync:GraphQL to specific Query fields.
mitigations.implementation_details: Field-level IAM resource ARNs on CognitoUnauthRole; keep updateDevice for the telemetry processor's role (needed for the subscription).

mitigations.content: Throttle migrations: reject migrateFirmware while a device already has a migration in progress, cap start-migration concurrency, and set a CodeBuild concurrent-build limit.
mitigations.implementation_details: Conditional update on migrationStatus in start-migration; ReservedConcurrentExecutions on start-migration; ConcurrentBuildLimit on the firmware project.

mitigations.content: Redact presigned URLs from logged OTA commands and shorten the presign expiry to the minimum the download needs.
mitigations.implementation_details: message-logger strips url/sigUrl/signerCertUrl from cmd/+/ota payloads; reduce PRESIGNED_URL_EXPIRY from 900 s.

mitigations.content: Enable ESP32 flash encryption and secure boot v2 so device keys and the PSK cannot be read back over USB (production guidance; accepted for the workshop).
mitigations.implementation_details: Document as production guidance in README security considerations; for the workshop treat device keys as attendee-extractable and rely on M3/M9.

mitigations.content: Make device identity revocable: enable CRLs on both Private CAs, revoke the device cert in the deregistrar, and have Mosquitto check the CRL (or an auth plugin that checks the registry).
mitigations.implementation_details: RevocationConfiguration CrlConfiguration Enabled with an S3 bucket; acm-pca RevokeCertificate in device-deregistrar; mosquitto crlfile refreshed by the entrypoint.

mitigations.content: Lock down the Builder-Pi GUI: require an operator token, add CSRF protection, make /api/config read-only at runtime, and bind the GUI away from the attendee AP interface.
mitigations.implementation_details: Flask before_request token check; drop POST /api/config or restrict to localhost; set gui_host to the operator interface rather than 0.0.0.0.

mitigations.content: Least-privilege Builder-Pi role: drop bucket-wide firmware read and registry Scan; the builder API returns a short-lived presigned URL for just the device being flashed.
mitigations.implementation_details: Remove s3:GetObject on bucket/* and dynamodb:Scan from BuilderPiSsmRole; extend the registrar response with a presigned merged.bin URL.

mitigations.content: Device identity is never in a firmware image: keys, certificates, CA roots and WiFi go into a separate certs NVS partition image built per device at registration, flashed by the Builder-Pi and then deleted from S3 (every version), with a 1-day lifecycle rule on identity/ as a backstop.
mitigations.implementation_details: Device-identity CodeBuild job writes identity/<serial>/certs.bin; Builder-Pi delete_identity() removes all versions after flashing; firmware loads identity from the certs partition (device_identity.cpp) and refuses one issued for another chip. Firmware images are built once per variant into shared/<version>/.

mitigations.content: Keep the WiFi PSK only in SSM: the device-identity CodeBuild job reads it as a PARAMETER_STORE environment variable, and the registry, registrar, prepare-build and migration state machine no longer store or pass it.
mitigations.implementation_details: DeviceIdentityProject env WIFI_PASSWORD Type PARAMETER_STORE; registrar writes no WiFi to the registry; the migration path pushes prebuilt shared images and has no build env.

mitigations.content: Limit the SSM hybrid activation: registration limit of 1, expiry of hours not 7 days, and auto-deregister stale managed instances.
mitigations.implementation_details: RegistrationLimit and ExpirationDate in the SSMActivation custom resource; setup-builder-pi-remote.sh already prunes ConnectionLost instances.

mitigations.content: Enforce broker hostname checks on devices: add stable DNS names as SANs on both broker certificates and enable wolfSSL domain-name checking.
mitigations.implementation_details: Matches the existing backlog item (stable broker DNS + SANs); wolfSSL_check_domain_name(ssl, MQTT_BROKER_ENDPOINT) before the handshake.

mitigations.content: Harden the build supply chain: pin base images by digest, pin oqs-provider/OpenSSL commits and package versions, verify Arduino index signatures, use npm ci with a lockfile, and deploy images by digest with immutable ECR tags.
mitigations.implementation_details: Dockerfile FROM ...@sha256; apt version pins; arduino-cli with signed indexes (data/*.json.sig exist); ECR ImageTagMutability IMMUTABLE with per-build tags.

mitigations.content: ECR scan on push for all three images.
mitigations.implementation_details: ImageScanningConfiguration ScanOnPush true on the ECR repositories.

mitigations.content: Improve broker availability: run at least two broker tasks across AZs, set Mosquitto connection limits, and rely on Shield Standard on the NLB.
mitigations.implementation_details: BrokerService DesiredCount >= 2 (check bridge client-id uniqueness), max_connections in mosquitto.conf.

mitigations.content: Make dashboard actions auditable: enable AppSync request logging and record caller identity once sign-in exists.
mitigations.implementation_details: AppSync LogConfig with FieldLogLevel ERROR/ALL to CloudWatch; include identity in start-migration logs.

mitigations.content: Narrow the bridge IoT policy to the device topic shapes (dt/esp32-*/telemetry, cmd/esp32-*/*) and remove the shadow wildcards it does not use.
mitigations.implementation_details: Edit policy_doc in the bridge provisioner Lambda.

mitigations.content: Fail-closed public-mirror curation: publish-public-mirror.sh strips .kiro/ and .threatmodel/, scrubs account IDs, the PSK and internal URLs, and aborts if any survive.
mitigations.implementation_details: Implemented in cloudformation/publish-public-mirror.sh (sweep step 4/5).

mitigations.content: Apply the same curation to the Workshop Studio source zip (package-workshop-src.sh), which currently ships .kiro/, .threatmodel/ and real account IDs.
mitigations.implementation_details: Reuse the mirror script's strip and sweep in package-workshop-src.sh.

mitigations.content: Track the remaining classical-only links (IoT Core bridge TLS 1.2, OTA download, Builder-Pi HTTPS) and move them to hybrid ML-KEM where AWS endpoints support it; explain them in the workshop as the next migration step.
mitigations.implementation_details: Workshop content note plus periodic check of AWS endpoint PQ TLS support.

mitigations.content: Mutual TLS required on both broker listeners, each trusting only its own Private CA, TLS 1.3 only.
mitigations.implementation_details: mosquitto.conf require_certificate true, use_identity_as_username true, per_listener_settings with separate cafile per listener.

mitigations.content: Telemetry processor only updates devices that were registered (attribute_exists(serialNumber)), so unknown things cannot create dashboard cards.
mitigations.implementation_details: Conditional UpdateItem in dashboard/lambda/telemetry-processor/index.py.

mitigations.content: Signed OTA verification when the command declares sigAlg: signer leaf must chain to the baked signer root (fails closed without a root), then the ECDSA-P256 or ML-DSA-44 signature must verify; signer keys are scrubbed from the build disk after signing.
mitigations.implementation_details: otaVerifyImage / otaVerifyChainToRoot in all three sketches; buildspec post_build signing. Bypassable while unsigned OTA is accepted (see M001).

mitigations.content: Broker runs in private subnets with no public IP; its task role can read only the named broker and bridge secrets.
mitigations.implementation_details: AssignPublicIp DISABLED; BrokerTaskRole GetSecretValue on explicit secret ARNs.

mitigations.content: start-migration validates the requested variant against an allow-list before starting a migration.
mitigations.implementation_details: VALID_VARIANTS check in raw_device_builder/lambda/start-migration/index.py.

mitigations.content: Separate code signing from device identity: the OTA signer certificates are issued only by two dedicated firmware-signing root CAs (ECDSA P-256 and ML-DSA-44) with the codeSigning EKU; the device trusts only the signing root matching the image's sigAlg, requires codeSigning on the signer leaf, and never trusts a device CA root for OTA.
mitigations.implementation_details: FirmwareSignerCA / MlDsaFirmwareSignerCA in broker-container-stack.yaml; issue_broker_certs.py issues the signers with CodeSigningCertificate/V1; identity format 2 carries sig_cls / sig_mldsa (read-only for the identity job); otaVerifyChainToRoot in ota_updater.cpp. Verified on pqc-a, Nov 4.

assumptions.description: Each workshop runs in a throwaway AWS account (Workshop Studio per-event account, or pqc-a/pqc-b test accounts) that is torn down after the event.

assumptions.description: The system holds no customer data, PII beyond optional dashboard identities, or regulated data; telemetry is synthetic device health data.
assumptions.impact: Disruption, not data theft, is the main business impact; this drives the risk ratings.

assumptions.description: Attendees are semi-trusted: many are security practitioners with physical access to a board, the Builder-Pi station and the workshop WiFi.
assumptions.impact: Device keys and the WiFi PSK are treated as extractable; controls must not depend on their secrecy.
assumptions.rationale: Room setup in the workshop documentation.

assumptions.description: Risk tolerance: a disrupted or visibly compromised live session at re:Invent is a reputational failure for a security workshop, so fleet-wide or cross-attendee attacks are not acceptable; single-device or workshop-scale availability issues are tolerable.
assumptions.impact: Threats whose only outcome is a degraded session at workshop scale may be accepted; anything that lets one attendee or an internet user take over other devices, or that would be copied into production designs, stays open.
assumptions.rationale: Business context: Medium criticality, Low financial impact, high reputational sensitivity.

assumptions.description: The public aws-samples repo is reference material; readers may reuse the design.
assumptions.impact: Production readers need the documented hardening (flash encryption, secure boot, sign-in, revocation) rather than copying the workshop defaults.

assumptions.description: Operator Admin credentials are short-lived Isengard credentials obtained via ada, and upstream sources are pinned to release tags.
assumptions.impact: Supply-chain and operator-mistake threats are rated Unlikely/Possible rather than Likely.
assumptions.rationale: Observed operator workflow and Dockerfile pins.

businessContext.description: Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration for IoT workshop (AWS Workshop Studio / re:Invent builders session, also published as the public aws-samples/sample-aws-iot-pqc sample). ESP32-S3 field devices connect over MQTT/TLS 1.3 with a hybrid SecP256r1MLKEM768 key exchange to a containerized Mosquitto PQC broker (ECS Fargate in private subnets behind an internet-facing NLB on 8883 classical / 8884 ML-DSA-44), which bridges over classical mTLS to AWS IoT Core. Two Private CAs (classical ECDSA P-256 and ML-DSA-44) issue broker and device certificates. A cloud pipeline (API Gateway + Lambda registrar, CodeBuild firmware builder container, Step Functions PQC migration, S3 presigned-URL OTA) builds each firmware variant once (no device data in the image), issues each device's identity into a separate certs flash partition and migrates devices classical -> PQC key exchange -> PQC certificates over the air. An on-site Raspberry Pi (Builder-Pi, managed via SSM hybrid activation) runs a Flask GUI that registers and USB-flashes devices and hosts the 2.4GHz workshop WiFi AP. A CloudFront + S3 React dashboard backed by AppSync, Cognito, DynamoDB and IoT Rules -> Lambdas shows live telemetry and sends LED/OTA commands. Deployed per event from a single master CloudFormation stack in a throwaway account. In scope: device firmware, broker, NLB, PKI, build/registration/OTA/migration pipeline, Builder-Pi, dashboard and their AWS resources. Out of scope: AWS-managed service internals, the physical venue network beyond the workshop AP, attendee laptops.

components.name: ESP32 field device firmware
components.specific_service: ESP32-S3 (XIAO) Arduino firmware, wolfSSL 5.7+, FreeRTOS
components.description: One modular sketch built as three variants: classical (ECDHE + ECDSA cert, port 8883), pqc (SecP256r1MLKEM768 + ECDSA cert, 8883), pqc-mldsa (ML-KEM + ML-DSA-44 cert, 8884). Identity (keys, certs, both CA roots, WiFi) is loaded at boot from the unencrypted certs NVS partition; an identity issued for another chip is refused. mTLS to the broker with WOLFSSL_VERIFY_PEER chain check only (no hostname/SAN check). Publishes dt/<thing>/telemetry and lifecycle, subscribes cmd/<thing>/+. Dual-boot OTA: downloads from the URL in the command over TLS with WOLFSSL_VERIFY_NONE (no server cert check), enforces the sha256 from the same command if present, and verifies an ECDSA-P256 or ML-DSA-44 signature ONLY when the command includes sigAlg; an OTA without sigAlg is installed unsigned in every variant. The signer leaf must chain to the firmware-signing root for the image's sigAlg (sig_cls / sig_mldsa, separate CAs from the device roots) and carry the codeSigning EKU.

components.name: Workshop WiFi access point
components.specific_service: NetworkManager AP on the Builder-Pi MediaTek USB radio
components.description: 2.4GHz WPA2-PSK AP built by the configure-wifi-ap SSM document from /pqc-workshop/wifi/*. One shared PSK for every device and attendee; the same PSK is written into every device's certs partition.

components.name: Builder-Pi edge host and Flask GUI
components.specific_service: Raspberry Pi, Flask app.py, arduino-cli/esptool, SSM agent, CloudWatch agent
components.description: Flask GUI bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 with NO authentication or CSRF protection. Routes: /api/register, /api/reflash, /api/deregister, /api/serial/<port>, /api/scan, GET/POST /api/config (POST merges arbitrary JSON into config incl. API endpoint/bucket/region). Calls the builder API with SigV4 using SSM hybrid-activation role credentials, downloads the shared firmware pieces and the device's identity image from S3, USB-flashes them, then deletes every version of the identity image.

components.name: Broker Network Load Balancer
components.specific_service: Elastic Load Balancing NLB pqc-broker-nlb (internet-facing)
components.description: Internet-facing NLB in public subnets. TCP listeners 8883 and 8884 pass TLS through to the broker (no termination). Broker SG allows 0.0.0.0/0 on both ports. VPC BPA exclusion (allow-bidirectional) lets IGW ingress through on BPA accounts.

components.name: Mosquitto PQC broker
components.specific_service: ECS Fargate service pqc-workshop-broker, Mosquitto + OpenSSL 3.5 + oqs-provider
components.description: Private subnets, no public IP, egress via NAT and VPC endpoints. Listener 8883 trusts the classical CA, 8884 the ML-DSA-44 CA; both require_certificate + use_identity_as_username, TLS 1.3 only. NO acl_file: any client holding any cert from the trusted CA can publish/subscribe to any topic. Loads broker and bridge credentials from Secrets Manager at startup. Logs connect/subscribe/publish events with client IDs and source IPs.

components.name: Mosquitto to IoT Core bridge
components.specific_service: Mosquitto bridge to AWS IoT Core MQTT data endpoint
components.description: Bridge client pqc-workshop-broker-bridge connects to IoT Core 8883 with an IoT-issued X.509 cert (TLS 1.2, AmazonRootCA1). Bridges dt/+/telemetry out and cmd/# in; lifecycle is NOT bridged. Its IoT policy allows publish dt/* and shadow, subscribe/receive cmd/* and shadow wildcards: one identity speaks for every device.

components.name: AWS IoT Core and rules
components.specific_service: AWS IoT Core message broker and Rules Engine
components.description: Rules: pqc_workshop_telemetry (dt/+/telemetry) and pqc_workshop_lifecycle (dt/+/lifecycle) -> telemetry-processor; pqc_workshop_message_log_dt (dt/+/+) and _cmd (cmd/+/+) -> message-logger; pqc_workshop_auto_register (lifecycle online) -> auto-register. Also hosts the IoT Things, esp32-pqc-device ThingType and per-device policies (devices do not connect to IoT Core directly).

components.name: Telemetry processor Lambda
components.specific_service: Lambda pqc-workshop-telemetry-processor
components.description: Updates pqc-workshop-devices only when the row already has serialNumber (registered-only guard), reconciles migrationStatus, and calls AppSync. Resource policy allows any IoT rule in the account (rule/*).

components.name: Message logger Lambda
components.specific_service: Lambda pqc-workshop-message-logger
components.description: Writes dt/+/+ and cmd/+/+ payloads to pqc-workshop-message-log (TTL) for the dashboard log view. cmd payloads include OTA commands with presigned URLs.

components.name: Auto-register Lambda
components.specific_service: Lambda pqc-workshop-auto-register
components.description: Creates IoT Things on a lifecycle 'online' event. Effectively dormant: lifecycle is not bridged from Mosquitto to IoT Core.

components.name: Builder API
components.specific_service: API Gateway REST pqc-workshop-device-builder-api, stage prod, EDGE (default)
components.description: Public edge endpoint. POST /register, /deregister, /firmware, all AuthorizationType AWS_IAM (SigV4). No resource policy, API key or usage plan. Caller is the Builder-Pi.

components.name: Device registrar Lambda
components.specific_service: Lambda pqc-workshop-device-registrar
components.description: Creates the IoT Thing and per-device policy, writes the registry (no WiFi), seeds the dashboard device row, and starts the device-identity CodeBuild job (which reads the WiFi from SSM itself). Returns 503 until the shared classical image exists. Role: iot:Create*/Attach* on *, iot:Publish cmd/*, SSM /pqc-workshop/* read.

components.name: Deregistrar and firmware-pusher Lambdas
components.specific_service: Lambdas pqc-workshop-device-deregistrar, pqc-workshop-firmware-pusher
components.description: Behind /deregister (removes Thing/cert/policy/registry/dashboard row) and /firmware.

components.name: Start-migration and prepare-build Lambdas
components.specific_service: Lambdas pqc-workshop-start-migration and pqc-workshop-prepare-build
components.description: start-migration (invoked by AppSync migrateFirmware) validates the variant and starts the state machine. prepare-build resolves the variant to its prebuilt shared image (shared/<version>/) from variants.json; no per-device build.

components.name: PQC migration state machine
components.specific_service: Step Functions STANDARD pqc-workshop-pqc-migration
components.description: PrepareBuild (resolves the shared image) -> SetStatusPushing -> PublishOta -> SetStatusRebooting; Catch -> SetStatusFailed. No build and no WiFi in the execution history.

components.name: Publish-OTA Lambda
components.specific_service: Lambda pqc-workshop-publish-ota
components.description: Presigns firmware.bin (+ .sig and signer.crt for signed variants) for 900 s and publishes {action: ota-update, url, sha256, sigUrl, signerCertUrl} to cmd/<thing>/ota at QoS 1 via IoT Core.

components.name: Firmware build CodeBuild
components.specific_service: CodeBuild pqc-workshop-firmware-build (firmware-builder ECR image)
components.description: Runs once per version per deployment: writes only build settings (variant, version, broker host/port) into secrets.h, compiles the modular sketch with arduino-cli, signs firmware.bin with the era signer key from Secrets Manager, and uploads to s3://firmware/shared/<version>/. A separate device-identity job issues both device certificates per device and writes identity/<serial>/certs.bin.

components.name: Broker and signer cert provisioner CodeBuild
components.specific_service: CodeBuild pqc-workshop-broker-cert-provisioner (cert-issuer ECR image)
components.description: Mints the classical and ML-DSA broker server certs and the classical and ML-DSA OTA signer identities from the two CAs and stores keys/certs in 12 Secrets Manager secrets.

components.name: Bridge provisioner Lambda
components.specific_service: Lambda pqc-workshop-bridge-provisioner (CloudFormation custom resource)
components.description: Creates the pqc-workshop-broker-bridge Thing, IoT keys/cert and wildcard bridge policy, downloads AmazonRootCA1, stores cert/key/root in Secrets Manager. Role has iot Create/Delete/Attach on *.

components.name: Classical Private CA
components.specific_service: ACM Private CA ROOT, EC_prime256v1 / SHA256WITHECDSA, CRL disabled
components.description: Trust root for the 8883 listener: issues the classical broker cert, classical/pqc device certs, and the classical OTA signer.

components.name: ML-DSA-44 Private CA
components.specific_service: ACM Private CA ROOT, ML_DSA_44, CRL disabled
components.description: Trust root for the 8884 listener: issues the ML-DSA broker cert, pqc-mldsa device certs and the ML-DSA OTA signer. Key held by ACM PCA (not self-managed).

components.name: Dashboard AppSync API
components.specific_service: AppSync GraphQL pqc-workshop-device-api, AWS_IAM auth
components.description: Queries listDevices/getDevice (devices table), getDeviceLog (message log), getBrokerLog (broker-log-reader). Mutations updateDevice (SETs arbitrary input fields on the device row), migrateFirmware (start-migration -> full build + OTA). sendCommand (command-publisher: led-on/led-off on cmd/<thing>/control, diag on cmd/<thing>/diag only; IAM limited to those topics). deleteDevice has no resolver. Subscription onDeviceUpdate.

components.name: Cognito identity pool
components.specific_service: Cognito Identity Pool pqc_workshop_dashboard, AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities true
components.description: No user pool. Anyone with the pool ID (shipped in the public dashboard config.json) gets guest credentials for CognitoUnauthRole, which allows appsync:GraphQL on the whole API.

components.name: Dashboard CloudFront distribution
components.specific_service: CloudFront distribution with OAC to the S3 hosting bucket
components.description: Public HTTPS (redirect-to-https, default cert), GET/HEAD only, no WAF, no access logging. Serves the Vite/React dashboard and its runtime config.json.

components.name: Dashboard web client
components.specific_service: React SPA in an attendee/operator web browser
components.description: Gets guest credentials from Cognito, SigV4-signs AppSync calls, polls every 5 s, offers the firmware picker / migrate button.

components.name: Broker log reader Lambda
components.specific_service: Lambda pqc-workshop-broker-log-reader
components.description: Reads /pqc-workshop/broker-container for the getBrokerLog query (client IDs, source IPs, topics).

components.name: SSM fleet management for the Builder-Pi
components.specific_service: SSM hybrid activation (Custom::SSMActivation) + 5 SSM Documents + Run Command
components.description: Hybrid activation (7-day code, in the Builder-Pi bundle and Secrets Manager iot/<instance>/*) registers the Pi. Run Command documents install the toolchain, deploy the app, configure services and the WiFi AP (decrypting the PSK). Two candidate Pi roles exist (<instance>-ssm-role and pqc-workshop-builder-pi-ssm).

components.name: Operator deploy workstation
components.specific_service: Laptop / Cloud IDE running deploy-workshop.sh, bundle-for-builder-pi.sh, setup-builder-pi-remote.sh
components.description: Holds Admin credentials; deploys the master CloudFormation stack, writes /pqc-workshop/* SSM params, starts image builds, generates the Pi bundle and orchestrates SSM provisioning.

components.name: Image and dashboard build CodeBuild projects
components.specific_service: CodeBuild image builds (broker, cert-issuer, firmware-builder, dashboard)
components.description: Build the broker, cert-issuer and firmware-builder container images (apt/Ubuntu mirror, oqs-provider) into ECR, and the Vite dashboard into the hosting bucket with a CloudFront invalidation. Supply-chain entry point.

components.name: NAT gateway and VPC endpoints
components.specific_service: VPC NAT gateway + VPC endpoints (ecr.api, ecr.dkr, secretsmanager, logs, s3)
components.description: Egress path for the private broker task to IoT Core, ECR, Secrets Manager and CloudWatch Logs. VPC flow logs enabled (14 days).

dataStores.name: Firmware S3 bucket
dataStores.description: pqc-workshop-firmware-<acct>: SSE-S3, versioning on, public access blocked. Holds sketch sources (source/), Pi app assets, and per device <serial>/<version>/ firmware.bin, firmware.merged.bin, bootloader, partitions, metadata.json, firmware.bin.sig, signer.crt. Every firmware image embeds that device's private key and the WiFi PSK, and old versions persist. Readable in full by the Builder-Pi role.

dataStores.name: Device registry table
dataStores.description: DynamoDB pqc-workshop-device-registry (SSE on): serial, thing name, cert metadata, firmware version/target, status, broker endpoint, and a PLAINTEXT wifiPassword. Readable by the Builder-Pi role (GetItem/Scan).

dataStores.name: Dashboard devices table
dataStores.description: DynamoDB pqc-workshop-devices (SSE on): per-device dashboard state, latest telemetry, migrationStatus. Read and freely updated through AppSync (updateDevice).

dataStores.name: Message log table
dataStores.description: DynamoDB pqc-workshop-message-log (SSE on, TTL, PITR on): MQTT payloads for dt/+/+ and cmd/+/+, including OTA commands that carry presigned firmware URLs.

dataStores.name: Secrets Manager secrets
dataStores.description: Default aws/secretsmanager key. pqc-broker/*: classical and ML-DSA broker CA/cert/key, classical and ML-DSA OTA signer CA/cert/key (pqc-broker/signer-*), IoT bridge cert/key/root CA; iot/<instance>/* SSM activation id/code.

dataStores.name: SSM Parameter Store /pqc-workshop/*
dataStores.description: iotEndpoint, broker/endpoint, wifi/ssid (String), wifi/password (SecureString, aws/ssm key), dashboard config. Written by deploy-workshop.sh.

dataStores.name: ECR repositories
dataStores.description: pqc-workshop-mosquitto-broker, pqc-workshop-cert-issuer, pqc-workshop-firmware-builder (scan on push, mutable latest tag). Images pulled by Fargate and CodeBuild by :latest.

dataStores.name: Dashboard hosting bucket
dataStores.description: Auto-named S3 bucket (SSE-S3, versioned), readable only by the CloudFront distribution via OAC. Content is public by design: the SPA and config.json, which includes the Cognito identity pool ID and AppSync endpoint.

dataStores.name: Build source buckets
dataStores.description: pqc-workshop-broker-source-<acct> (broker and cert-issuer build sources, buildspecs) and pqc-workshop-dashboard-source-<acct>. SSE-S3, versioned. Writing here changes what CodeBuild builds.

dataStores.name: CloudWatch log groups
dataStores.description: /pqc-workshop/broker-container (7 d; client IDs, source IPs, topics), /aws/codebuild/pqc-workshop-firmware-build and cert-provisioner, /pqc-workshop/builder-pi, Lambda logs, VPC flow logs (14 d). Default encryption.

dataStores.name: ESP32 device flash
dataStores.description: Device private keys, certificates, both CA roots and the WiFi PSK in the certs NVS partition (0x721000), separate from the app image. No flash/NVS encryption or secure boot, so anyone with the board can read them over USB.

threatActors.name: Insider
threatActors.description: A team member or contractor with repo or account access (GitLab, Workshop Studio, pqc-a/pqc-b) who abuses it. Covers the disgruntled-employee case.

threatActors.name: External Attacker
threatActors.description: An external attacker who has read the public aws-samples repo, so knows the architecture, topic layout, resource names and the anonymous Cognito/AppSync design, and targets a live workshop deployment during an event window. Can abuse AppSync migrateFirmware to start CodeBuild builds and OTA pushes, tamper with dashboard state, and read message/broker logs.

threatActors.name: Nation-state Actor
threatActors.description: Harvest-now-decrypt-later adversary recording TLS traffic for future quantum decryption. This is the workshop's teaching premise rather than a realistic target: the telemetry has little intelligence value. Relevant mainly to confirm classical-only links (bridge TLS 1.2, Builder-Pi HTTPS, OTA download) are understood.

threatActors.name: Hacktivist
threatActors.description: A group wanting a visible stunt at a high-profile event, e.g. defacing or disrupting the live re:Invent PQC demo or showing the 'post-quantum' devices can be hijacked.

threatActors.name: Organized Crime
threatActors.description: Criminals who find the anonymous AppSync API or leaked operator/Pi credentials and abuse the account for cost (repeated CodeBuild firmware builds via migrateFirmware, compute) or pivot using the Admin-level operator role. Workshop data itself has little resale value.

threatActors.name: Competitor
threatActors.description: No competitive value in an open-source educational sample.

threatActors.name: Script Kiddie
threatActors.description: Automated internet scanning and commodity tooling. Finds the internet-facing NLB on 8883/8884, the public builder API and the CloudFront dashboard; can pull the Cognito identity pool ID from the public config.json and call the anonymous AppSync API (list/overwrite devices, trigger migrations). Mostly blocked at the broker by mTLS.

threatActors.name: Disgruntled Employee
threatActors.description: Covered by TA001 Insider for this system.

threatActors.name: Privileged User
threatActors.description: The workshop operator or sample maintainer making a mistake with Admin credentials: deploying into the wrong account, leaking the Builder-Pi bundle (7-day SSM activation code), committing real account IDs/PSK, or publishing internal content (.kiro/, .threatmodel/) to the public mirror.

threatActors.name: Supply-chain compromise
threatActors.description: A compromised upstream the build trusts: the Ubuntu apt mirror and oqs-provider/OpenSSL sources in the broker and firmware-builder image builds, Arduino ESP32 core and library indexes, npm packages in the dashboard build, uvx/npx-fetched tooling, and mutable :latest ECR tags. Malicious code would run with CodeBuild role access to the CAs, signer keys and firmware bucket.

threatActors.name: Terrorist Organization
threatActors.description: A group with limited offensive cyber capability, primarily using the internet for propaganda and recruitment

threatActors.type: Private Sector Offensive Actor / Cyber Mercenary
threatActors.name: Private Sector Offensive Actor
threatActors.description: No high-value individual targets in this system.

threatActors.name: Curious or malicious on-site attendee
threatActors.description: A workshop attendee (often a security practitioner) in the room with legitimate physical access to an ESP32 board, the Builder-Pi USB station and the workshop WiFi, plus the public dashboard. Can dump their own board's flash over USB to recover its device private key and the shared WiFi PSK, join the AP, drive the unauthenticated Builder-Pi GUI on :8080, connect to the broker with their extracted cert and publish to other devices' cmd/<thing>/ota or dt topics (no broker ACLs), and call the anonymous AppSync API to migrate or overwrite other attendees' devices. Motive is curiosity, a demo of skill, or disrupting the session; impact is a broken workshop in front of an audience.

crossingPoints.description: Device joins the workshop AP with the shared WPA2 PSK.
Device MQTT/TLS 1.3 to the internet-facing NLB on 8883/8884. NLB is TCP passthrough; no auth at the NLB, SG open to 0.0.0.0/0.
NLB to Mosquitto. Broker enforces mTLS (require_certificate, CA per listener) but has NO topic ACLs, so any authenticated device can act on any topic.
Broker downlink (OTA, control) to devices over their TLS sessions. Device verifies the broker chain only, no hostname/SAN check; topic origin is not authenticated.
Bridge publishes dt/+/telemetry to IoT Core with its IoT cert (wildcard dt/* policy); broker logs to CloudWatch via the task role.
IoT Core delivers cmd/# to the bridge subscription (wildcard cmd/* policy).
Broker task reads its secrets and pulls its image via VPC endpoints (task/execution roles scoped to named secrets and repo).
Telemetry processor calls AppSync with its IAM role.
Browser loads the SPA from CloudFront and gets UNAUTHENTICATED Cognito guest credentials whose role allows appsync:GraphQL on the whole API. Effectively anonymous access to all queries and mutations.
AppSync resolvers read/update the devices table and message log and invoke the broker log reader via service roles. No per-caller authorization: updateDevice SETs any field on any device.
AppSync migrateFirmware invokes start-migration; API Gateway invokes registrar/deregistrar/firmware-pusher. Authorization inherited from the (anonymous) AppSync caller or the SigV4 Pi caller.
Device-management Lambdas and the state machine start firmware builds (WIFI_PASSWORD as plaintext env), read SSM WiFi params, and presign firmware objects.
Registrar/deregistrar/publish-OTA/state machine create and delete IoT Things and policies, publish cmd/<thing>/ota, and write the devices table.

Device downloads OTA firmware from the URL in the command with TLS server verification disabled (WOLFSSL_VERIFY_NONE). The 900 s presigned URL is a bearer token for the legitimate path. Integrity relies on the command's sha256 and, only for commands that declare sigAlg, the signature check.
Builder-Pi calls the builder API with SigV4 using its SSM-rotated role credentials.
Builder-Pi reads the whole firmware bucket (every device's key-bearing image) and /pqc-workshop/* SSM params including the WiFi PSK.
Builder-Pi GetItem/Scan on the device registry (includes plaintext wifiPassword).
Builder-Pi CloudWatch agent writes /pqc-workshop/builder-pi.
esptool flashing and serial console over USB. Physical access only, no authentication.
Anyone on the workshop AP can reach the Builder-Pi Flask GUI on :8080 over plain HTTP with no authentication or CSRF protection.
Pi SSM agent registers with the hybrid activation code (7-day validity) and polls SSM.
SSM Run Command executes provisioning documents as root on the Pi.
Operator (Admin) writes SSM params, build sources and starts image builds; SSM stores the activation code in Secrets Manager.
Dashboard build syncs the SPA and config.json into the hosting bucket and invalidates CloudFront.
Bridge provisioner creates the bridge Thing, keys and wildcard policy in IoT Core.

assets.description: Stable per-era classical (ECDSA P-256) and ML-DSA-44 signer private keys in Secrets Manager (pqc-broker/signer-*). Whoever holds them can sign firmware every device will accept.

flows.description: Build generates key + CSR in-container and gets the cert from ACM PCA, then writes key and cert into secrets.h.
Device key leaves the build embedded in firmware.bin / merged.bin and is stored, versioned, in the firmware bucket.
Firmware with the device key and PSK is flashed to the board; flash is not encrypted, so the key can be read back over USB.
Device proves possession of its key in the mTLS handshake. Broker accepts any cert from the listener's CA and then allows any topic.
Provisioner mints signer identities and stores the keys in pqc-broker/signer-*.
Firmware build reads the era signer key to sign firmware.bin, then scrubs it from disk. Any code running in the build (incl. a poisoned builder image) can read it.
Provisioner requests broker and signer certificates from both CAs.
Firmware build requests device certificates from either CA; the CodeBuild role is the only routine issuer.
Broker task loads its server keys and the bridge key at startup via VPC endpoints.
Bridge authenticates to IoT Core with its key; one identity covers all device traffic.
Operator writes the PSK as a SecureString.
Registrar copies the PSK into the registry in PLAINTEXT.
State machine passes the PSK to CodeBuild as a PLAINTEXT env var; visible in execution history and build details. It is then compiled into every firmware image.
configure-wifi-ap decrypts the PSK onto the Pi to bring up the AP; the Pi role can also read it at any time.
Build uploads firmware.bin, merged.bin, .sig and signer.crt to <serial>/<version>/.
Builder-Pi downloads merged.bin for USB flashing; its role can read every device's image.

Device downloads the OTA image over TLS WITHOUT server certificate verification (WOLFSSL_VERIFY_NONE). It checks the sha256 supplied in the same command and, only if the command declares sigAlg, the signature chained to the baked signer root. Removing sigAlg from the command downgrades the update to unsigned.
Publish-OTA publishes the ota-update command (presigned URLs) to cmd/<thing>/ota.
Command reaches the device via the bridge and Mosquitto. Because the broker has no ACLs, any connected device could inject a forged OTA command on the same topic.
Message logger stores OTA commands (with presigned URLs) in the message log, readable through anonymous AppSync getDeviceLog.
Device publishes telemetry to the broker.
Telemetry processor writes telemetry to the dashboard table (registered-only guard). Anonymous AppSync updateDevice can overwrite the same fields.
Browser obtains guest credentials with no sign-in.
Guest credentials authorize every AppSync query and mutation, including migrateFirmware and updateDevice.
SSM hybrid activation issues and rotates the Pi's role credentials.
Pi uses its credentials to call the builder API; anyone driving the unauthenticated GUI effectively borrows them.

residualRiskAssessments.rationale: No sign-in exists; any internet user can trigger builds and OTA pushes. Fix with M004 and M006 before the next public event.
updateDevice is callable anonymously and falsifies the workshop's PQC evidence. M005 is a low-cost fix.

Resolved by the NVS identity design (M012): firmware images are built once per variant and carry no keys, certificates or WiFi PSK, so a leaked presigned URL discloses only public code. Presigned URLs in the message log remain an anonymous-read issue under T004 / M004 / M007.
Anonymous read of logs and payloads; low data value but closes with M004.

Accepted for the workshop: boards are handed to attendees and flash/NVS encryption and secure boot would complicate re-flashing. The identity now lives only in the board's certs partition (never in firmware images, and deleted from S3 once flashed), so extraction is limited to the attendee's own board; the firmware refuses an identity issued for another chip, which stops copying a certs image onto another board but not reuse of an extracted key. The design must not rely on key secrecy (see T006, T008, T024), and M008 is documented as production guidance.
Any attendee can install arbitrary firmware on any device. Highest priority: M001 (fail-closed signature) and M003 (broker ACL), then M002.
mTLS limits this to cert holders, but without ACLs any attendee can spoof others' telemetry. Closes with M003.
No revocation path; impact bounded by the throwaway account lifetime but extracted keys stay valid for the whole event. M009 needed.
Anyone on the AP can manage every device on the station. M010 is low cost.
Runtime config changes can redirect flashing to attacker firmware. M010.

No longer fleet-wide: shared firmware images hold no keys, and each identity image is deleted (every version) after flashing with a 1-day lifecycle backstop. A Pi compromise still exposes identities in flight and can mint new ones through /register. M011 (scope GetObject to shared/* and identity/*), M010 and M009 reduce it further.
Registration limit 5 and multi-day expiry still allow a leaked bundle to add rogue instances. Tighten per M014.

Resolved (M013): the PSK lives only in SSM as a SecureString. The device-identity CodeBuild job reads it as a PARAMETER_STORE variable, and the registrar, registry table, prepare-build and migration state machine no longer store or pass it. The remaining copies are by design: the Builder-Pi (it runs the AP), each device's certs partition, and the identity image until it is flashed.
Rogue AP plus no hostname check enables MITM in the room. M015 (already a backlog item).
Release-tag pins reduce but do not remove the risk; impact is fleet-wide. Track M016.
Requires an insider or compromised principal; scan on push detects known vulnerabilities only. Track M016.
Reserved concurrency of 5 limits fan-out but builds still queue. Closes with M004 and M006.
Accepted at workshop scale: a single task is enough for tens of devices and the event is short; M018 recorded for production use.
No attribution is possible today. Closes with M004 and M019.
Bridge wildcard policy amplifies a broker compromise; private subnet reduces exposure. M020 is a low-cost fix.
Public mirror is protected (M021); the Workshop Studio source zip is not (M022).

Accepted: short-lived workshop data has no long-term secrecy value, and firmware images no longer carry keys. The classical links are part of the teaching story (M023); moving the OTA download to hybrid ML-KEM is a planned change (S3 supports it).
Signed pushes are protected by M026, and images no longer carry keys, but the unverified TLS still exposes unsigned pushes. M001 and M002.

Resolved (M029): the OTA signers are issued only by two dedicated firmware-signing root CAs, with the codeSigning EKU. Devices trust only the signing root that matches the image's sigAlg and require codeSigning; device CA roots are used for TLS only. Verified on pqc-a hardware: an OTA signed with a device-CA certificate was refused (no chain to sig_cls), and one signed with a signing-root certificate lacking codeSigning was refused (no EKU). Residual: theft of a signer key from Secrets Manager or the build (T015, T016).

softwareProfile.description: ESP32 Arduino firmware (wolfSSL TLS 1.3 + ML-KEM, FreeRTOS WiFi/MQTT tasks, dual-boot OTA) plus an AWS backend: ECS Fargate Mosquitto/OpenSSL 3.5 + oqs-provider broker, NLB, ACM Private CA, Lambda, Step Functions, CodeBuild, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito, DynamoDB, S3, CloudFront, IoT Core, SSM, Secrets Manager. Raspberry Pi edge host running a Flask GUI with pyserial/esptool (it never compiles firmware). MIT-0 licensed sample.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Device private keys and certificates
dataAssetProfiles.description: Per-device ECDSA P-256 and ML-DSA-44 key pairs and certificates issued at registration by the device-identity CodeBuild job, written to the device's unencrypted certs NVS partition (the S3 copy is deleted after flashing), and used for device-to-broker mTLS.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Private CA signing keys
dataAssetProfiles.description: Signing keys of the two workshop trust roots (classical ECDSA P-256 Private CA and the ML-DSA-44 CA). Compromise allows minting trusted broker or device identities.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Broker server and IoT bridge credentials
dataAssetProfiles.description: Broker TLS server certificates/keys (classical and ML-DSA) and the AWS IoT Core bridge client certificate/key, stored in Secrets Manager and loaded by the Fargate broker task.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Workshop WiFi credentials
dataAssetProfiles.description: Workshop AP SSID and PSK. Source of truth is SSM SecureString /pqc-workshop/wifi/password; also written into each device's certs partition by the device-identity job and configured on the Builder-Pi AP.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Firmware images
dataAssetProfiles.description: Shared firmware binaries, one per version (classical / PQC / PQC+ML-DSA / ML-DSA-signed), in the versioned firmware S3 bucket under shared/<version>/, flashed by the Builder-Pi and delivered to devices over OTA via presigned S3 URLs. Images carry no keys, certificates or WiFi; integrity determines what code runs on the device.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Device telemetry and message log
dataAssetProfiles.description: JSON telemetry on dt/<thing>/telemetry (heap, RSSI, firmware version, negotiated PQC group, TLS version) plus lifecycle events, stored in DynamoDB (pqc-workshop-devices, pqc-workshop-message-log) and pushed to the dashboard. Its integrity is what proves to attendees that a device negotiated ML-KEM.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Device commands and OTA jobs
dataAssetProfiles.description: Downlink messages on cmd/<thing>/+ (LED control, OTA trigger carrying a presigned firmware URL, revert-to-classical). A forged OTA command can make a device install attacker-chosen firmware.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Device registry and migration state
dataAssetProfiles.description: DynamoDB device registry (serial, thing name, cert metadata, firmware version, status) and dashboard device rows (migrationStatus), plus IoT Thing / per-device policy records.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Dashboard user accounts
dataAssetProfiles.description: Cognito user pool identities (email address, password) and issued JWTs used to call the AppSync API that reads telemetry and sends device commands and migrations.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Infrastructure-as-code and deployment configuration
dataAssetProfiles.description: CloudFormation templates, buildspecs, Dockerfiles, SSM documents, deploy scripts and the Builder-Pi bundle (contains a 7-day SSM hybrid activation code). Public on GitHub after scrubbing; integrity determines what is deployed.

userPersonas.name: Workshop operator
userPersonas.description: Deploys and tears down the master stack with Admin credentials, provisions the Builder-Pi over SSM, and runs readiness checks.

userPersonas.name: Workshop attendee
userPersonas.description: Plugs in and flashes a device at the Builder-Pi, joins the workshop WiFi, and uses the dashboard (Cognito) to watch telemetry and trigger PQC migrations. Physically present with access to the hardware and the venue network.

userPersonas.name: ESP32 field device
userPersonas.description: Authenticates to the broker with an mTLS client certificate; publishes dt/<thing>/* and subscribes to cmd/<thing>/*; downloads OTA firmware from presigned S3 URLs.

userPersonas.name: Builder-Pi edge host
userPersonas.description: On-site Raspberry Pi registered as an SSM managed instance (pqc-workshop-builder-pi-ssm role). Calls the builder API to register devices, downloads firmware from S3, flashes over USB, and runs the open Flask GUI on :8080 and the workshop WiFi AP.

userPersonas.name: Mosquitto broker and IoT bridge
userPersonas.description: Fargate task that terminates device PQC TLS and bridges to AWS IoT Core with its own client certificate (pqc-workshop-broker-bridge Thing).

userPersonas.name: Cloud workload roles
userPersonas.description: Lambda (registrar, deregistrar, prepare-build, publish-ota, start-migration, telemetry-processor, command-publisher, auto-register), CodeBuild (firmware build, image build, cert-issuer) and Step Functions roles that create IoT Things/policies, issue certificates and publish OTA.

userPersonas.name: Unauthenticated internet or venue user
userPersonas.description: Can reach the internet-facing NLB (8883/8884), the CloudFront dashboard and the builder API endpoint, and anyone in RF range or on the venue LAN can attempt the workshop AP and the Builder-Pi GUI.

userPersonas.name: Sample maintainer
userPersonas.description: Commits to the internal GitLab repo and publishes the scrubbed public mirror to GitHub aws-samples and the Workshop Studio source zip.

nonFunctionalRequirements.rationale: ESP32-S3 RAM/flash budget must fit wolfSSL with ML-KEM and ML-DSA plus dual OTA partitions.
Needed only for the duration of a workshop event; not a production service.
Recovery is a from-scratch redeploy of the master stack (roughly an hour).
Must deploy in one attempt from CloudFormation and scripts with minimal documented manual steps.
Must work in accounts with and without VPC Block Public Access.
MQTT 3.1.1, TLS 1.3, IANA SecP256r1MLKEM768 group, FIPS 203/204 algorithms, X.509.
Device WiFi/MQTT tasks auto-reconnect; single broker task and NLB.
Dual-boot partitions allow rollback to classical firmware after a failed migration.
Tens of devices per workshop room.
Demo devices drive only an LED.
